findings.issue_text: **What's wrong:** Whenever `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` this returns one page too many. A group with exactly 50 members (default limit 50) reports `1/2`; a group with 100 reports pages `1..3`.

**Why it matters:** `showingLast` is never true on the real last page, so `next` stays enabled and navigates to a page that renders an empty member list, and the "1/2" counter is simply wrong. Since paginated membership is the headline feature of this PR, this is user-visible on the first group anyone opens with a round member count.

**How to fix:** `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`. Also clamp `next` (`admin-group.js.es6:40-48`) to `(totalPages - 1) * limit` rather than to `user_count`, otherwise the final `next` still lands on an offset past the last full page.
`app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:90`

**What's wrong:** `CollectionAssociation#delete` given an Integer resolves it with `find(records)` *scoped to the association*, which raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` if the id is not in the group.

**Why it matters:** Any stale admin tab, double-click on the remove "×", or concurrent removal produces an error response instead of a no-op. The base branch explicitly tested this case ("succeeds silently when removing non-members") and that spec was deleted along with the behavior. `removeMember` in the JS has no error handler, so the failure is silent in the UI and the list never refreshes.

**How to fix:** Look the membership up first and no-op if absent, e.g. `user = group.users.find_by(id: user_id); group.remove(user) if user` (using the model's own `remove` also keeps you on the supported path — see #3).
`app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:90`

**What's wrong:** `has_many :through` `delete` uses the `delete_all` strategy on the join rows by default, so any `GroupUser` callbacks / counter caches (`groups.user_count` is a real column surfaced by `BasicGroupSerializer` and the admin list) are not run.
**Why it matters:** If `user_count` is maintained by callbacks, this leaves the admin group list showing stale counts after every removal.
**How to fix:** The add path correctly uses `group.add(user)`; the remove path should symmetrically use `group.remove(user)`. Verify against `app/models/group.rb` (not present in this checkout).
`app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22-23`

**What's wrong:** `/groups/:name/members.json?limit=1000000` serializes a million users in one request. `?limit=-1` or `?offset=-1` produces `OFFSET/LIMIT must not be negative` from Postgres → `StatementInvalid` → 500.
**Why it matters:** Attacker-tunable DoS and a 500 reachable by anyone who can see the group.
**How to fix:** `limit = [[params[:limit].to_i, 1].max, 100].min` (with a default when absent) and `offset = [params[:offset].to_i, 0].max`.
`app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:67-71`
**What's wrong:** `params.require(:usernames)` may be an `Array` (any client sending `usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b`), and `Array#split` doesn't exist → `NoMethodError`.
**Why it matters:** 500 on a legitimate, conventional request encoding.
**How to fix:** Normalize: `Array(usernames).join(",").split(",").map(&:strip).reject(&:blank?)`.
`app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71-75`
**What's wrong:** Returns `success_json` even if none of the submitted usernames resolved. Previously a bad username surfaced through `group.usernames=` validation.
**Why it matters:** Combined with #7, the admin types a typo, clicks Add, and nothing at all happens.
**How to fix:** Return the list of usernames that could not be added (or 422) and surface it client-side.
`app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:40-60`, `admin-group.js.es6:60-64`

**What's wrong:** `removeMember`/`addMembers` have no rejection handler, and the controller discards the returned promise. Every other action in this controller (`save`, `destroy`) uses `bootbox.alert` on failure. Also `findMembers` (`group.js:21`) now `return ;` on empty name and is no longer returned from either route's `setupController`.
**Why it matters:** A 422 from the server is invisible to the admin; load failures are swallowed rather than reaching the route error handler, and callers can no longer chain.
**How to fix:** Add `.catch(popupAjaxError)` / `bootbox.alert` handlers; return the promise from `setupController`.
**What's wrong:** After adding members the selector still shows them.
**Why it matters:** The obvious next action (add more) re-submits the previous names. This is an unfinished user-facing path, not a nice-to-have.
**How to fix:** Clear the `usernames` property in the success handler.
`app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb`, `config/routes.rb:49-50`, `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb`
**What's wrong:** Three separate contract breaks land silently:

`GET /groups/:name/members.json` changes from a bare JSON array to `{members: [...], meta: {...}}`, *and* now defaults to 50 rows where non-automatic groups previously returned everything. Any plugin or external consumer both mis-parses and silently truncates.
`PATCH /admin/groups/:id` with `changes: {add:, delete:}` is deleted outright.
`POST /admin/groups` and `PUT /admin/groups/:id` move from nested `group: {...}` params to top-level params.
**Why it matters:** Third-party plugins and API clients break with no warning; the truncation failure is silent.
**How to fix:** At minimum a release note; ideally the `members` endpoint keeps the old array shape when no `limit`/`offset` is supplied, or the old param nesting is accepted alongside the new.

**What's wrong:** There is no spec anywhere for `GroupsController#members`, the most substantially rewritten action (pagination, new response envelope, `total`). Also missing: removing a non-member (see #2), adding a non-existent username (the base branch had this test and it was dropped), and limit/offset bounds. No JS tests for `totalPages`/`currentPage`, which is where bug #1 lives.
**Why it matters:** The two critical bugs above would have been caught by the tests that were deleted or never written.
**How to fix:** Add request/controller specs for `members` pagination and the missing edge cases; add a JS unit test for the page arithmetic.

**What's wrong:** The automatic-group tests use hard-coded `group_id: 1`/`id: 1`, relying on seed data for the `admins` auto group and mutating it. And `xhr :put, :remove_member` uses PUT while the route is `delete "members"`.
**Why it matters:** Seed-dependent tests are brittle; controller specs bypass routing so the wrong verb passes but documents the API incorrectly.
**How to fix:** Use `Fabricate(:group, automatic: true)`; use `xhr :delete`; consider a routing spec for the two new member routes.

`app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:22-25` sets only `name` and `visible`, but `group.hbs` shows the alias-level combo box on the new-group form and `asJSON` sends it (`models/group.js:62-68`). The admin's selection is dropped and only takes effect after a second save. (Pre-existing, but the new form makes it more visible.)

`app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:38` — `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` means any PUT omitting `visible` flips the group invisible. Fine for the one known client, hostile for API users; prefer `if params.key?(:visible)`.

`app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:73-77` — `add` persists immediately on a saved record, so a subsequent `save` failure reports an error after the members are already added. Same pattern in `remove_member`.

The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **Why it matters:** `showingLast` is never true on the real last page, so `next` stays enabled and navigates to a page that renders an empty member list, and the "1/2" counter is simply wrong. Since paginated membership is the headline feature of this PR, this is user-visible on the first group anyone opens with a round member count.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces pagination math that is off by one when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`. `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, so for 100 users with limit 50 it yields 3 instead of 2. `showingLast` compares `currentPage` to this incorrect `totalPages`, so on the real last page (`offset=50` => `currentPage=2`) `showingLast` is false and `next` remains enabled. Clicking `next` sets `offset` to `min(offset+limit, user_count)` which becomes 100, and `findMembers()` requests `offset=100`, which the server will return as an empty `members` list (since it does `limit(limit).offset(offset)`), matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **How to fix:** `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`. Also clamp `next` (`admin-group.js.es6:40-48`) to `(totalPages - 1) * limit` rather than to `user_count`, otherwise the final `next` still lands on an offset past the last full page.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `admin-group.js.es6`, `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which overcounts when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g., 100 users, limit 50 => returns 3 pages instead of 2). Additionally, `actions.next` clamps the new offset to `user_count` (`Math.min(offset+limit, user_count)`), which can set `offset` to an out-of-range value equal to `user_count` (e.g., from 50 -> 100). `Group.findMembers` then uses that offset (it only clamps to `<= user_count`), causing the final page to fetch an empty member list. Clamping to the last valid page start (e.g., `(totalPages-1)*limit` or `Math.max(0, user_count - limit)`) would avoid this.

There is no rescue/handling here, so a stale/malicious `user_id` can turn this endpoint into a 500 error instead of a clean success/422 response. This behavior is directly introduced by the diff (previous code removed by username and didn’t call `delete` with a raw id).

**How to fix:** Look the membership up first and no-op if absent, e.g. `user = group.users.find_by(id: user_id); group.remove(user) if user` (using the model's own `remove` also keeps you on the supported path — see #3).

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member` does `group.users.delete(user_id)`. In Rails, calling `delete` on an association with an id is already a safe no-op when the associated record/join doesn’t exist; it does not raise just because the user isn’t a member. Therefore the suggested “look up first and no-op if absent” is not addressing a verifiable bug introduced by this diff, but rather an unnecessary/alternative implementation detail.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, membership removal is implemented as `group.users.delete(user_id)` followed by `group.save`. For a typical `has_many :users, through: ...` association, `collection.delete` removes join rows using a direct delete (`delete_all` on the join) rather than instantiating the join model, so any join-model callbacks and counter-cache maintenance on the join (`GroupUser`) will not run. The previous code path used `group.remove(user)`, which strongly suggests there is intended encapsulated logic for removals (likely including bookkeeping such as user counts). So this diff plausibly introduces stale `user_count`/missing side-effects when removing members.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **Why it matters:** If `user_count` is maintained by callbacks, this leaves the admin group list showing stale counts after every removal.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly reloads members (and total count) after a removal. `Discourse.Group#removeMember` issues the DELETE then calls `self.findMembers()`, and `findMembers()` sets `user_count` from `result.meta.total` via `setProperties({ user_count: ..., members: ... })`. So the client-side `user_count` used in the admin UI is refreshed immediately after each removal, not left stale. Any claim about DB-level callbacks/counter caches affecting the admin groups index is not verifiable from this diff, and the UI here is already updating `user_count` from the server response.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the new `Admin::GroupsController#add_members` uses the higher-level API `group.add(user)`, while the new `#remove_member` removes membership via `group.users.delete(user_id)`. This is a behavioral change from the prior code (removed in this diff) which used `group.remove(user)` for deletions. Using the association `delete` can bypass whatever logic `group.remove` encapsulates (callbacks, counters, side effects), making the asymmetry a plausible correctness defect introduced by the change. The existence/intent of `group.remove` is evidenced by its use in the deleted `update_patch` method within this same diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22-23`

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the new pagination params are taken directly from the request: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i`. There is no validation/clamping. Because `to_i` preserves negatives (e.g. "-10" -> -10), a request with a negative `offset` can be passed into `group.users...offset(offset)`, which in Rails/ActiveRecord can raise an error (offset must be >= 0), resulting in a 500. Similarly, `limit` is unbounded and can be set extremely large, which is a potential performance/DoS issue on a public endpoint guarded only by `ensure_can_see!`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **What's wrong:** `/groups/:name/members.json?limit=1000000` serializes a million users in one request. `?limit=-1` or `?offset=-1` produces `OFFSET/LIMIT must not be negative` from Postgres → `StatementInvalid` → 500.

adjudication.rationale:
In `GroupsController#members`, the new code trusts `params[:limit]`/`params[:offset]` directly:

```rb
limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i
offset = params[:offset].to_i
members = group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)
```

There is no server-side clamping/validation. A request like `/groups/:name/members.json?limit=1000000` will attempt to fetch/serialize up to a million users (potential DoS/perf issue). Likewise `limit=-1` or `offset=-1` will be passed through to SQL as negative `LIMIT/OFFSET`, which Postgres rejects (“must not be negative”), raising an exception that typically becomes a 500. This is a verifiable defect introduced/left in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **Why it matters:** Attacker-tunable DoS and a 500 reachable by anyone who can see the group.
**How to fix:** `limit = [[params[:limit].to_i, 1].max, 100].min` (with a default when absent) and `offset = [params[:offset].to_i, 0].max`.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff introduces `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` and then applies them directly to `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)`. There is no clamping/validation: a client can supply an extremely large `limit` (potential DoS via heavy query/serialization) or a negative `offset` (e.g. `-10`), which can lead to invalid SQL/DB errors depending on the adapter. The JS client bounds offset, but server-side cannot rely on that, so the proposed clamping is addressing a real defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:67-71`
**What's wrong:** `params.require(:usernames)` may be an `Array` (any client sending `usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b`), and `Array#split` doesn't exist → `NoMethodError`.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code does `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` and then unconditionally calls `usernames.split(",")`. In Rails, a client can legitimately supply `usernames` as an Array (e.g., `usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b`), in which case `params[:usernames]` will be an `Array`. `Array` does not respond to `split`, so this would raise a `NoMethodError` and likely result in a 500. The diff does not add any type check/coercion to prevent this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **Why it matters:** 500 on a legitimate, conventional request encoding.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code does `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` and then unconditionally calls `usernames.split(",")`. If the client sends a conventional Rails-style array encoding for repeated values (e.g. `usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b`, which yields `params[:usernames]` as an Array), `split` will raise `NoMethodError`, causing a 500. The diff introduces this strict string-only handling without type checking/coercion.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **How to fix:** Normalize: `Array(usernames).join(",").split(",").map(&:strip).reject(&:blank?)`.

adjudication.rationale: Real correctness issue: `Admin::GroupsController#add_members` does `usernames.split(",")` and then `User.find_by_username(username)` without stripping whitespace or rejecting blanks. If the client sends usernames like `"bob, alice"` (note the space) or includes trailing commas, the lookup for `" alice"` / `""` will fail and intended users won’t be added. The proposed normalization addresses this by trimming and removing blanks (and also tolerating array input).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71-75`
**What's wrong:** Returns `success_json` even if none of the submitted usernames resolved. Previously a bad username surfaced through `group.usernames=` validation.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In the new `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, submitted usernames are split and each is looked up with `User.find_by_username`; missing usernames are simply skipped. The action then calls `group.save` and returns `success_json` if the group saves, even if **zero** users were actually added (e.g., all usernames were invalid). In the previous implementation, membership changes could go through `group.usernames = ...` (in `create` / `update_put`), which would typically validate/raise errors for bad usernames rather than silently succeeding. This diff therefore introduces a behavior where typos/unknown usernames can result in a 200 success with no effect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **Why it matters:** Combined with #7, the admin types a typo, clicks Add, and nothing at all happens.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In the new `addMembers` flow, the client just calls `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"))` and does not handle success/failure or show any message. On the server, `Admin::GroupsController#add_members` silently ignores unknown usernames (`User.find_by_username(username)` check) and still returns `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds (which it typically will even if no users were added). Result: if the admin types a typo/nonexistent username and clicks Add, the UI refreshes members but no change occurs and no error is shown—i.e., “nothing happens.”

adjudication_records.issue_text: **How to fix:** Return the list of usernames that could not be added (or 422) and surface it client-side.

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, the code iterates `usernames.split(",")` and only adds users when `User.find_by_username(username)` returns a user; unknown/typoed usernames are silently ignored. The action still returns `success_json` (200) as long as `group.save` succeeds, even if none or only some of the requested usernames were actually added. This makes the endpoint report success for a partial/no-op operation and provides no way for the client to inform the admin which usernames failed, matching the finding’s concern.

The diff changes `afterModel` hooks that returned `model.findMembers()` promises into `setupController` calls that just invoke `model.findMembers();` without returning/awaiting the promise (e.g. `admin_group_route.js`, `discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6`). adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb`, `config/routes.rb:49-50`, `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb`
**What's wrong:** Three separate contract breaks land silently:

adjudication.rationale: The proposed finding is too vague to verify against the diff: it asserts “Three separate contract breaks” but does not name which APIs/contracts, what the expected vs new behavior is, or point to specific lines. While the diff does include potentially contract-affecting changes (e.g., `Group#findMembers` now returns `undefined` when name is empty instead of a resolved promise/array, and request/response payload shapes changed in tandem with the server), the finding as written does not identify any specific, checkable defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `GET /groups/:name/members.json` changes from a bare JSON array to `{members: [...], meta: {...}}`, *and* now defaults to 50 rows where non-automatic groups previously returned everything. Any plugin or external consumer both mis-parses and silently truncates.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (which would return a bare array of serialized users) to `render json: { members: ..., meta: { total, limit, offset } }`, and it now always applies pagination: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `members = ...limit(limit).offset(offset)` for *all* groups (previously only automatic groups were limited/offset; non-automatic groups returned the full list). This is a backwards-incompatible API/contract change for `GET /groups/:name/members(.json)`: existing consumers expecting an array will mis-parse, and consumers expecting a complete member list will now only get the first 50 unless they implement pagination.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `PATCH /admin/groups/:id` with `changes: {add:, delete:}` is deleted outright.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the incremental PATCH-specific logic (`update_patch`) and the controller no longer branches on `request.patch?`; membership changes are now handled via new dedicated endpoints (`PUT /admin/groups/:group_id/members` and `DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members`) with corresponding client-side calls (`addMembers`, `removeMember`). There is no evidence in the diff of remaining code that still sends `PATCH /admin/groups/:id` with `changes: {add/delete}` or expects that behavior, so this is an intentional API change/refactor rather than a verifiable defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `POST /admin/groups` and `PUT /admin/groups/:id` move from nested `group: {...}` params to top-level params.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change the payload shape: the client-side `Discourse.Group#asJSON()` is updated from `{ group: {...} }` to a flat object, and `Admin::GroupsController#create`/`update` are updated to read `params[:name]`, `params[:visible]`, etc. Tests are also updated to post top-level params. Since both sides (caller and controller) are changed consistently in this diff, this is an intentional API change, not a verifiable bug/defect introduced within the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **Why it matters:** Third-party plugins and API clients break with no warning; the truncation failure is silent.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` to always paginate and to return a different JSON shape. Previously it rendered a plain serialized array of members (`render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)`), and only applied limit/offset for automatic groups (defaulting to 200). Now it defaults to `limit = 50` for all groups and returns `{ members: ..., meta: { total, limit, offset } }`. Any third-party plugin/API client expecting the old response (an array) will break, and clients that don’t implement pagination may silently see only the first 50 members (truncation) without an error. This is directly verifiable from the controller change in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **How to fix:** At minimum a release note; ideally the `members` endpoint keeps the old array shape when no `limit`/`offset` is supplied, or the old param nesting is accepted alongside the new.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` from returning a bare serialized array (`render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)`) to returning an object with `{ members: ..., meta: ... }` unconditionally. Any existing client (internal code not updated here, or external integrations) calling `/groups/:id/members` and expecting the old top-level array will break even when no `limit`/`offset` is supplied. The new JS code was updated to expect `result.members`/`result.meta`, but the endpoint itself is no longer backward compatible, so the finding about needing a release note or backward-compatible response/params is a verifiable issue introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **What's wrong:** There is no spec anywhere for `GroupsController#members`, the most substantially rewritten action (pagination, new response envelope, `total`). Also missing: removing a non-member (see #2), adding a non-existent username (the base branch had this test and it was dropped), and limit/offset bounds. No JS tests for `totalPages`/`currentPage`, which is where bug #1 lives.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does substantially rewrite `GroupsController#members` (pagination and a new `{members, meta}` JSON envelope), and the only spec file touched is `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb`, which does not add coverage for `GroupsController#members`. However, the proposed finding is primarily about *missing tests* (“no spec anywhere”, “no JS tests”), which is not a verifiable runtime/correctness defect in the diff itself, and “no spec anywhere” cannot be proven from this diff alone (tests could exist elsewhere). The other points (non-member removal, non-existent usernames, bounds) are likewise framed as missing tests rather than demonstrated bugs introduced by the change.

The diff shows tests being refactored and new ones added (e.g., for .create, .update, .add_members), not simply deleted or “never written.” While the spec file does appear truncated at the end (an actual, specific issue), the finding does not point to that or any specific failing behavior; it only makes a generic claim about missing tests catching unspecified bugs.

While the diff does add new pagination logic/endpoints, the absence of extra edge-case specs or JS unit tests is not a verifiable bug/security/correctness problem in the code itself, and the finding doesn’t point to a specific failing behavior. adjudication_records.issue_text: **What's wrong:** The automatic-group tests use hard-coded `group_id: 1`/`id: 1`, relying on seed data for the `admins` auto group and mutating it. And `xhr :put, :remove_member` uses PUT while the route is `delete "members"`.
matched_golden_ids: The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The golden issue is that the test uses `xhr :put` for `remove_member` but the route expects a DELETE request (`delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member'`). The candidate explicitly identifies this same HTTP method mismatch (PUT vs DELETE), even though it also mentions an additional, separate concern about hard-coded IDs/seed data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **Why it matters:** Seed-dependent tests are brittle; controller specs bypass routing so the wrong verb passes but documents the API incorrectly.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces member-management routes under /admin/groups/:group_id with specific verbs: `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` and `put "members" => "groups#add_members"` (config/routes.rb). However, the updated controller spec begins a `.remove_member` context and calls `xhr :put, :remove_member, group_id: 1, ...`, i.e., it uses PUT for `remove_member`, which conflicts with the route expecting DELETE. Because controller specs invoke actions directly (not through routing), this wrong verb can still pass while misrepresenting the real API. Additionally, multiple specs hardcode `id: 1` / `group_id: 1` to represent an automatic group (e.g., update ignores name change; add_members cannot add to automatic groups), which is seed/fixture dependent and brittle if the automatic group with id 1 differs or doesn’t exist.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **How to fix:** Use `Fabricate(:group, automatic: true)`; use `xhr :delete`; consider a routing spec for the two new member routes.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff adds admin routes `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` and `put "members" => "groups#add_members"`. But in the new controller spec under `context ".remove_member"`, the test uses `xhr :put, :remove_member, group_id: 1, ...`, which does not match the route/HTTP verb (should be DELETE). Also it hardcodes `group_id: 1` to represent an automatic group, which is not verifiable/stable in the spec; using `Fabricate(:group, automatic: true)` would make the test correct and deterministic. The “routing spec” note is optional, but the verb/id issues are real defects introduced in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:22-25` sets only `name` and `visible`, but `group.hbs` shows the alias-level combo box on the new-group form and `asJSON` sends it (`models/group.js:62-68`). The admin's selection is dropped and only takes effect after a second save. (Pre-existing, but the new form makes it more visible.)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In the diff, the new-group form (`admin/templates/group.hbs`) renders the alias-level combo box even when the group has no `id` (i.e., on create). The client model’s `asJSON()` (`discourse/models/group.js`, new version) includes `alias_level`, and `create()` POSTs `data: this.asJSON()` to `/admin/groups`. However the new `Admin::GroupsController#create` only assigns `name` and `visible` (and never reads `params[:alias_level]`), so any alias-level selection made during creation is ignored and the group is created with the server default. Only a later PUT to `update` would apply `alias_level`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:38` — `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` means any PUT omitting `visible` flips the group invisible. Fine for the one known client, hostile for API users; prefer `if params.key?(:visible)`.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `Admin::GroupsController#update`, the code unconditionally assigns `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"`. If a client sends an update request without the `visible` param (common for partial updates / API usage), `params[:visible]` is `nil`, the expression evaluates to `false`, and the group will be saved as invisible. This is a behavior change/regression compared to the prior PATCH path (`update_patch`) which did not touch `visible` at all; now PATCH/PUT both go through this method and will flip visibility when `visible` is omitted. Guarding with `if params.key?(:visible)` would avoid this defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:73-77` — `add` persists immediately on a saved record, so a subsequent `save` failure reports an error after the members are already added. Same pattern in `remove_member`.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code loops and calls `group.add(user)` for each username, then decides whether to return success based on `if group.save`. Since `group` is an already-persisted record (`Group.find`), membership changes performed by `group.add` (and in `remove_member`, `group.users.delete(user_id)`) will hit the DB immediately and are not rolled back if the subsequent `group.save` fails. That means the action can respond with an error even though members were already added/removed, and `group.save` is also not actually validating the membership operations themselves. The same non-atomic pattern exists in `remove_member`.
